description:
Read and edit the workspace's translation glossary and translation rules (Settings → Translation). Every translation in the workspace follows them: captions translate, translated videos and articles. Use it when the user says how a term must be translated, that a product or brand name must stay untranslated, or how translations into a language should read (tone, formality). Do NOT hand-edit translated captions or text for this instead: the next translation repeats the mistake.

Glossary terms: `original` (source text) → `translated` (the original itself keeps it as is), for `languages` (codes or names; omit for every language), optionally `case_sensitive`.
Rules: ONE per language: `prompt` (instructions the translator follows), optional `title` and `examples` [{original, translation}].

Changes are WORKSPACE-WIDE and apply to translations made after them: tell the user when you add or change one, and translate again (captions action "translate") what should pick them up.

action:
  • list        — {terms: [{term_id, original, translated, languages, case_sensitive}], term_count, rules: [{rule_id, title, language, prompt, examples}]}; `language` keeps what applies to it, `query` filters terms by text (at most 200 terms per reply)
  • set_term    — add a term or change one. An existing term is not overwritten: you get error "entry_exists" with `current`; show the user both, confirm, then call again with replace: true. Several terms with the same original → error "several_terms": pass the `term_id` you mean.
  • remove_term — delete the term with this `original` (exact text) or `term_id`
  • set_rule    — set `language`'s rule; an existing one needs replace: true after the user confirmed (same "entry_exists" reply)
  • remove_rule — delete `language`'s rule

Editing needs an editor or admin role, and saving needs a plan with the translation glossary (Enterprise); a refusal says which: tell the user, don't retry.

case_sensitive.description: set_term: match only this exact casing (default false; unchanged on a replace).

examples.description: set_rule: example translations the rule follows.

language.description: set_rule/remove_rule: the target language (code or name); list: keep what applies to it.

languages.description: set_term: target language codes or names; [] for every language. Omitted: every language on a new term, unchanged on a replace.

original.description: set_term/remove_term: the term as written in the source language.

prompt.description: set_rule: the instructions for this language.

query.description: list: keep terms whose text contains this.

replace.description: set_term/set_rule: overwrite an existing entry, only after the user confirmed.

term_id.description: set_term/remove_term: one term from list, when several share an original.

title.description: set_rule: a label (default the language name).

translated.description: set_term: what the term becomes in the translation.

name: translation_glossary
title: Translation glossary and rules
